title: The pattern of European work: short sets, quick flights
summary: Freeman describes 20 to 45 minute sets with local rhythm sections, German jazz clubs, and an eleven-minute closing spot at Hanover.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: With the Dutchmen College Band, I do about two 20-

minutes sets a night, and not so long ago I went over to Hanover to do the impressario called and said, would you want to come over and close a show. A big jazz concert with a lot of wellknown people in Europe and I went over and there was 11 minutes left for me. They paid me before I went on, I did the 11 minutes and caught a plane back to London, the same day. It's incredible, but I love the way of life here.

I, of course, the United States is a beautiful country, but I just don't know that the opportunities for a jazz soloist are there because the evidence of all this lies in seeing all the best soloists coming over here to work. But then again I haven't been in the States in three and a half years, so I don't know if the work is there or not.
